transcript.content: Hi, it’s good to meet you. What brings you in today?

Well… I came in because it’s gotten to where I can’t just sit at home and let them do this to me anymore. My in-laws, they keep acting like it’s just family disagreements, like I’m being “too sensitive” or making a fuss, but I know it’s more than that. They’re not just arguing with me. They’ve been using the altar, and people in the parish committee, to push me out little by little.

And it’s not only about the church, you know, it’s about everything I’ve done for this family being erased. Like they want everyone to forget that I was there, that I helped, that I gave my time and kept things together. They smile in front of people, but behind it there’s this… plan, this way they’re making me look like I don’t belong. That’s why I’m here. I need someone to understand that this isn’t just a normal family fight.
Are you certain that your in-laws are deliberately trying to push you out?

Yes. I mean, I know how that sounds when I say it plainly, but yes, I’m certain. This isn’t just me taking offense over one comment or one bad Sunday. It’s the way it keeps lining up — the things said at the altar, the way people on the parish committee suddenly look past me or act like I haven’t done anything, the way my in-laws present themselves like they’re innocent while little by little I’m being made to seem like I don’t belong.

I came in because I knew they weren’t just arguing with me. They were using the altar and the parish committee to push me out, to make everyone forget what I’ve done for this family. And I have done a lot. I was there, I helped, I gave my time, I held things together. So when they act like I’m imagining it, that almost makes it worse, because I can see what they’re doing. It’s deliberate.
Have you been hearing voices when no one is there?

Yes… yes, I have. Not all the time, but on several nights I heard my mother’s voice — my late mother — and it was very clear to me. It wasn’t like just remembering her, you know, like when you think of someone and you can almost hear how they used to talk. This was more like she was there, telling me where to put the marigolds and the candles.

And I know that sounds strange, but it felt… specific. She wasn’t just saying random things. It was about how things should be arranged, where they belonged. And one time I saw her, too, standing near the kitchen doorway. I told my husband, and he said no one was there, but I saw her there for that moment. It shook me, but it also felt like she was trying to guide me.
Have you been feeling depressed most of the day nearly every day?

Yes… most days, yes. It’s like after all that energy left me, I started waking up with this heavy sadness sitting on me before I even get out of bed. I don’t mean just being upset for an hour or having a bad morning. It feels like there’s no joy left in the house, and no joy left in me either.

I’ll open my eyes and it’s already there, that heaviness, like the whole place has gone quiet in a bad way. Things that should feel warm or familiar just don’t. I keep thinking about how much has been taken from me, how everything feels emptied out, and then the day just stretches ahead like something I have to get through. So yes, I would say I’ve been feeling depressed like that most of the day, nearly every day.
Do you believe you have done something terribly wrong or deserve to be punished?

Yes… I do. I don’t always say it that plainly, because it sounds awful, but yes, I keep thinking I must have done something terribly wrong. Like I ruined everything somehow — for my family, for the parish, for everyone who had trusted me or expected me to keep things together.

And then it spreads to even small things. If something breaks, or someone doesn’t call, or a plan falls apart, I start thinking, well, maybe that’s what I deserve. Maybe that’s my punishment for not doing things right, or for letting everything become such a mess. I know other people might say those little things just happen, but in my mind they feel connected to me, like proof that I failed and now I’m paying for it.
Have the voices or visions ever happened when you were not feeling depressed?

No… not really. The voices, and seeing my mother that one time, that was all during that period when I was hardly sleeping and I was rushing around, feeling like I had this very important duty — like I had to get the altar right, fix it, make it proper. It felt urgent then, like I couldn’t rest until everything was arranged the way it was supposed to be.

When my mood dropped afterward, I was still very guilty and sad — terribly sad — and I kept blaming myself, but I wasn’t hearing her voice anymore, and I wasn’t seeing her. It was more like the sadness and guilt stayed, but those clear voices and visions had stopped.
During that period when you hardly slept and felt driven to fix the altar, did you feel unusually high, energized, or irritable?

Yes… yes, I did. At the time I didn’t think of it as “high,” exactly, but there were days when I felt so bright and certain, like everything was finally clear to me. I had this feeling that I knew what needed to be done, especially with the altar, and that nobody else understood how important it was.

And then if anyone questioned me — even gently, even if they were just asking why I was doing something a certain way — I would feel this heat rise up in me. I’d snap at them. It felt like they weren’t just questioning the altar, they were insulting my whole family, my mother, everything I was trying to protect or set right. I know that sounds like a lot now, but in the moment it felt completely justified, like they were the ones being disrespectful.
During that period when you hardly slept and felt driven, did other people say your behavior was so unusual that you needed to be taken to a hospital?

I don’t think anyone said it in exactly those words at first, like, “She needs a hospital,” but… they were frightened by how unlike myself I was. I had always been the one who kept track of things — the parish preparations, the lists, the little details, the house, meals, laundry, all of that — and during that time I just couldn’t keep up with any of it properly.

The festival things especially… I thought I was helping, I thought I was doing something important, but really I stopped being able to manage the preparations in any normal way. My family had to step in and take over tasks I normally would have handled myself, because I was getting so wrapped up and not finishing things sensibly.

And at home it was the same. My husband started staying close to me more, almost watching over me, because I was missing meals, forgetting ordinary routines, not taking care of myself reliably. I don’t like admitting that, because I’ve always tried to be dependable, but yes… people could see something was very wrong.
Have you ever had voices, visions, or strong beliefs that people were plotting against you during a time when your mood was neither unusually high nor depressed?

No… I don’t think so. Not when I was just sort of normal in my mood, if that’s what you mean. The voices, and seeing my mother — that happened during that one time when I was barely sleeping and I was rushing around, feeling so certain that I had this duty, like I had to fix the altar and make it right. It all felt very urgent then, like I couldn’t stop or rest because something important was depending on me.

Later, when I came down from that and my mood dropped, I still felt awful — guilty, sad, like I had done something wrong or failed somehow — but I wasn’t hearing her voice anymore, and I wasn’t seeing her. Those parts had stopped. So no, I can’t really say I’ve had that when my mood was neither up like that nor depressed.
Did there come a time when your mood was unusually elevated or irritable for you?

Yes, there did. I mean… looking back, it was very unlike me. At the time I would have said I was just focused, or that I finally understood what needed to be done, but it was more than that.

There were days when I felt almost bright inside, like everything was sharp and clear and I was completely certain about the altar — what was wrong with it, what had to be fixed, how important it was. I didn’t really question myself. It felt like I had this… conviction, like I was the only one seeing it properly.

And then if anyone asked me about it, even just a normal question, I would get so irritated. I’d snap at them. It felt personal, like they weren’t just questioning what I was doing with the altar, they were insulting my family, my mother, all of it. I know now that was a lot to put onto a simple question, but in the moment it felt completely real and justified.
